cross_references.label: Authentication of a Writing — Foundation Requirement
cross_references.note: §1400 is the general authentication requirement that §§1450-1454 operate as presumptions within. When a §1450-1454 presumption is rebutted, the proponent falls back to §1400(a) extrinsic evidence.

cross_references.label: Authentication Required for Admission
cross_references.note: §1401 requires authentication before admission. A document that fails §1450-1454 and cannot satisfy §1400(a) is inadmissible under §1401.

cross_references.label: Official Records Hearsay Exception
cross_references.note: §1280 provides the hearsay exception for official records. §1450/1451 establish authenticity; §1280 establishes admissibility for the truth of the content. Both are needed to fully admit an official government record.

cross_references.label: Presumptions — Burden of Proof
cross_references.note: §600 et seq. governs California's rebuttable presumption framework. The §§1450-1454 presumptions are rebuttable under §600's framework — once the opponent introduces evidence to the contrary, the presumption is defeated and the burden shifts back to the proponent.

cross_references.label: Federal Self-Authentication
cross_references.note: FRE 902 is the federal analog, with a broader list of self-authenticating categories including certified electronic records (FRE 902(13)/(14) added 2017). California lacks an electronic self-authentication equivalent, making electronic records in California state court dependent on §1400(a) or §1552.

cross_references.label: Computer Printouts — Electronic Records Pathway
cross_references.note: §1552 provides an authentication pathway for computer-generated records in California, partially filling the gap left by the absence of a FRE 902(13)/(14) equivalent. Used together with §§1450-1454 for electronic official records.
